mainTopic: The crossing of the ירדן and the story of the מרגלים: their mission, names, כלב and יהושע, and the greatness of חברון
overview: This עמוד finishes the debate about how high the water of the ירדן piled up when the Jewish people crossed, giving two ways to explain it. Then the גמרא turns to the story of the מרגלים. ריש לקיש shows that sending the spies was משה's own choice, not ה׳'s command. רבי חייא בר אבא shows from the word חפר that the people's real goal was to shame ארץ ישראל. רבי יצחק and רבי יוחנן explain that some spies' names hint at their sins. רבא teaches that כלב went alone to חברון to pray at the graves of the אבות, while יהושע was already protected by משה's prayer in his new name. The גמרא then explains the names of the giants in חברון. It shows that even rocky חברון was seven times more fruitful than צוען, the best place in מצרים. The עמוד ends by quoting the פסוק about the spies' return, which the next עמוד explains.

steps.title: First explanation: camp formation versus one after another
steps.stepSummary: One אמורא explains the dispute about the height of the water. According to רבי יהודה, the people crossed in their camp formation. According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, they crossed one after another.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יהודה, they crossed in the same formation as their camp. According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, they crossed one after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining why רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון give such different heights for the piled-up water of the ירדן. This first opinion says they disagree about how the people walked across.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole camp crossed side by side, like the way they camped, the crossing was quick, so the water only needed to pile up a little (רבי יהודה's smaller number). If they crossed in a line, one after the other, the crossing took much longer, so the water had to pile up much higher (רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's huge number).

keyTerms.meaning: in the same formation as they camped
one after the other, in a line

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a sentence. The words 'they crossed in their camp formation' belong to רבי יהודה's view, which was started just before.

phrases.english: they crossed in the formation of their camping.
According to the words of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon —
they crossed one after the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה עָבְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the dispute about the height of the water at the ירדן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two תנאים disagree about how the people crossed: in camp formation (רבי יהודה) or in a line (רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון).

steps.title: Second explanation: who moves faster, people or water
steps.stepSummary: A second אמורא says both agree the people crossed in camp formation. They disagree about whether people move faster than water or water moves faster than people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another one says: according to both of them, the people crossed in their camp formation. One holds that a person moves faster, and the other holds that water moves faster.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different explanation of the same dispute. Here both sides agree about how the people walked, and they argue about speed instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people move faster than flowing water, the water does not need to pile up very high before everyone is across (רבי יהודה). If water moves faster than people, the water keeps piling up higher while the people are still crossing (רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון). So the difference in height comes from speed, not from how they lined up.

keyTerms.meaning: and the other one said, introducing a second explanation
according to both this master and that master

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the dispute about the water: either they disagree about how the people crossed (formation versus a line), or they agree on the formation and disagree about whether people or water move faster.

phrases.english: And one said:
Both according to this Master and according to that Master
they crossed in the formation of their camping.
One Master holds: a person is quick,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה, who gave the smaller height.

phrases.english: and the other Master holds: water is quick.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר בֵּין מָר וּבֵין מָר כַּחֲנִיָּיתָן עָבְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation of the same dispute that step 1 explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both agree on camp formation. The dispute is whether people or water move faster.

steps.title: Sending the spies was משה's own choice
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads 'שלח לך' as 'send on your own judgment.' ה׳ did not command the sending of the spies, because nobody chooses a bad portion for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Send you men.' ריש לקיש said: 'Send you' means on your own judgment. Would anyone choose a bad portion for himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic, the story of the מרגלים. ריש לקיש explains that the words 'שלח לך' mean ה׳ was leaving the decision to משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'לך' ('for you') shows that this was for משה's sake and by his choice. ריש לקיש backs this up with logic: ה׳ knew the spies would speak badly about the land, and no one picks something bad for himself. So it could not have been ה׳'s own command.

keyTerms.meaning: on your own judgment, by your own decision

phrases.english: “Send you men”
Reish Lakish said:
“Send you” means on your own judgment.
For would this person choose
a bad portion for himself?
phrases.notes: 'This person' is a respectful way of speaking about ה׳, who knew how the spies would turn out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. It follows naturally from the spies' cluster of grapes mentioned earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The spies were sent by משה's choice, not by ה׳'s command.

steps.title: Support from 'it was good in my eyes'
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in דברים supports ריש לקיש. משה says the plan was good 'in my eyes', meaning in his own eyes and not in ה׳'s.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what is written: 'And the matter was good in my eyes.' ריש לקיש said: 'In my eyes,' and not in the eyes of the Omnipresent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק that supports what ריש לקיש just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When משה retells the story in דברים, he says the idea seemed good 'in my eyes.' ריש לקיש points out that משה says 'my' eyes on purpose, which shows ה׳ did not approve the idea. This fits his reading of 'שלח לך.'

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what is written, bringing a supporting פסוק
the Omnipresent, a name for ה׳

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
“And the matter was good in my eyes.”
Reish Lakish said: “In my eyes,”
and not in the eyes of the Omnipresent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a supporting פסוק for ריש לקיש's reading in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That sending the spies was משה's decision and not ה׳'s command.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 1:23, 'ויטב בעיני הדבר', read as 'in my eyes' only.

steps.title: The real aim of the spies was to shame the land
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא says that when the people asked for spies to 'search' the land, their real intention was to shame ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'That they may search the land for us.' רבי חייא בר אבא said: the spies intended only to shame ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about why the people asked to send spies. רבי חייא בר אבא says the goal was to put the land to shame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface, 'ויחפרו' means 'search out.' רבי חייא בר אבא says the hidden purpose was to make the land look bad. He proves this in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: that they may search, which can also hint at shame

phrases.english: “That they may search the land for us”
Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said:
The spies intended nothing
other than the shame of Eretz Yisrael.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְרַגְּלִים לֹא נִתְכַּוְּונוּ אֶלָּא לְבוֹשְׁתָּהּ שֶׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the spies with a new teaching about their intention.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people's request for spies was really meant to shame ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Proof from the word 'חפר' in ישעיהו
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא links 'ויחפרו' to 'וחפרה הלבנה' in ישעיהו, where the word means being ashamed. So 'ויחפרו' hints at shame.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written here: 'That they may search the land for us,' and it is written there: 'And the moon will be ashamed and the sun will be embarrassed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for רבי חייא בר אבא's teaching by connecting the same word in two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ישעיהו, the root חפר clearly means shame, because it stands next to 'בושה'. Since the same root appears in 'ויחפרו', it carries that hint of shame here too. This shows what the people really intended.

keyTerms.meaning: it is written here, and it is written there, linking two פסוקים by a shared word

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש teaches that sending the spies was משה's idea and not ה׳'s command. רבי חייא בר אבא teaches, from the shared word חפר, that the people's goal in asking for spies was to shame ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: It is written here:
“That they may search the land for us,”
and it is written there:
“And the moon will be ashamed”
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 24:23. Here the same root חפר clearly means shame.

phrases.english: and the sun will be embarrassed, etc.”

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״וְיַחְפְּרוּ לָנוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״וְחָפְרָה הַלְּבָנָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the textual proof for רבי חייא בר אבא's claim in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That 'ויחפרו' hints at shaming the land.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 24:23, where 'וחפרה' stands next to 'ובושה' and means shame.

steps.title: The spies' names reflect their deeds: סתור בן מיכאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק passes on a tradition that each spy's name hints at his actions. He says only one example has reached him: סתור בן מיכאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And these are their names: from the tribe of ראובן, שמוע son of זכור.' רבי יצחק said: We have a tradition from our fathers that the spies were named after their deeds. But we only know the meaning of one name, 'סתור son of מיכאל.' He is called סתור because he undid the works of הקב״ה. He is called מיכאל because he made himself (or Him) weak.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the list of the מרגלים. רבי יצחק says their names hint at their sins, and he explains one name as an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a name is not random. It can tell you about the person's actions. סתור is read as 'tearing down' what הקב״ה did, and מיכאל is read as related to 'weak.'

keyTerms.meaning: A tradition handed down from earlier generations

phrases.english: "And these are their names: from the tribe of Reuven,
Shammua son of Zakkur."
Rabbi Yitzchak said:
This matter is a tradition we have from our fathers:
The spies were named after their deeds.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָנוּ לֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדֵינוּ אֶלָּא אֶחָד:
phrases.english: But we have only managed to figure out one:
"Sesur son of Michael."

phrases.aramaic: ״סְתוּר״ — שֶׁסָּתַר מַעֲשָׂיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
phrases.english: "Sesur": because he undid the works of the Holy One, Blessed be He.
"Michael": because he made himself weak.
phrases.notes: Literally 'himself,' but it can be read as pointing to ה׳: he made ה׳ seem too weak to give them the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: דָּבָר זֶה מָסוֹרֶת בְּיָדֵינוּ מֵאֲבוֹתֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the מרגלים, moving from their intentions to the meaning of their names.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names of the מרגלים hint at their deeds. סתור means he undid הקב״ה's works, and מיכאל means he made himself (or Him) weak.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן adds another name: נחבי בן ופסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds a second example of a spy's name that hints at his sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: We can also explain 'נחבי son of ופסי.' He is called נחבי because he hid the words of הקב״ה. He is called ופסי because he stepped over the ways of הקב״ה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן builds on רבי יצחק's tradition. He offers his own explanation for another spy's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק said he knew only one name. רבי יוחנן shows the same method works on a second name. נחבי sounds like 'hid,' and ופסי sounds like 'stepped over.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אַף אָנוּ נֹאמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: We too can say:
"Nachbi son of Vofsi."

phrases.aramaic: ״נַחְבִּי״ — שֶׁהֶחְבִּיא דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
phrases.english: "Nachbi": because he hid the words of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

phrases.aramaic: ״וׇפְסִי״ — שֶׁפִּיסַּע עַל מִדּוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
phrases.english: "Vofsi": because he stepped over the ways of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אַף אָנוּ נֹאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second name using the same method as רבי יצחק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נחבי hid הקב״ה's words, and ופסי stepped over הקב״ה's ways.

steps.title: Why does the verse say 'he came' instead of 'they came'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that the פסוק switches from plural ('they went up') to singular ('he came to חברון') and asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'They went up into the south, and he came to חברון.' It should have said 'and they came'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out an odd word in the פסוק. This question sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the spies went up together, so we would expect 'they came.' The singular 'he came' suggests that only one person went to חברון. The גמרא wants to know who that was and why.

phrases.english: "They went up into the south, and he came to Chevron."
phrases.notes: במדבר 13:22. Notice the switch from 'they' to 'he.'

phrases.english: It should have said "and they came"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new פסוק about the spies' journey.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the פסוק use the singular 'he came' when the whole group traveled?

steps.title: כלב went alone to pray at the graves of the אבות
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the singular word refers to כלב. He left the group and went to the graves of the אבות to pray that he would not be pulled into the plan of the מרגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This teaches that כלב separated himself from the plan of the spies. He went and lay down on the graves of the אבות. He said to them: 'My fathers! Ask for mercy for me so that I will be saved from the plan of the spies.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question about 'he came.' The 'he' is כלב, who went to חברון by himself to pray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The singular word shows that one person broke away from the group. That person was כלב. He was afraid of being pulled into the spies' plan, so he asked the אבות buried in חברון to pray for him.

phrases.english: Rava said: This teaches
that Calev separated himself from the plan of the spies,
and went and lay himself down on the graves of the forefathers.
He said to them: My fathers!
Ask for mercy for me
so that I will be saved from the plan of the spies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁפֵּירַשׁ כָּלֵב מֵעֲצַת מְרַגְּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the singular 'he came.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The singular refers to כלב, who went alone to חברון to pray at the graves of the אבות.

steps.title: Why יהושע did not need to go: משה already prayed for him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why יהושע did not join כלב. משה had already prayed for him, which is hinted at in the name change from הושע to יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for יהושע, משה had already asked for mercy for him, as the פסוק says: 'And משה called הושע son of נון, יהושע.' This means: 'May ה׳ save you from the plan of the spies.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question it never asks out loud: why didn't יהושע also go to pray? Its answer is that משה had already prayed for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה added a letter to הושע's name to make it יהושע. The new name is read as two parts, יה‎ (ה׳) and יושיע (will save). So the name itself is a prayer that ה׳ save him from the spies.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא never asks 'why not יהושע?' out loud. It just answers it. Don't look for a question in the text; it is assumed from the previous step.

phrases.aramaic: יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כְּבָר בִּקֵּשׁ מֹשֶׁה עָלָיו רַחֲמִים,
phrases.english: As for Yehoshua, Moshe had already asked for mercy for him,
as it says: "And Moshe called
Hoshea son of Nun, Yehoshua."
May ה׳ save you from the plan of the spies.
phrases.notes: The name יהושע is split into יה (ה׳) and יושיע (will save).

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כְּבָר בִּקֵּשׁ מֹשֶׁה עָלָיו רַחֲמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the hidden question raised by step 10: why only כלב went.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יהושע was already protected by משה's prayer, hinted at in the name יהושע.

steps.title: A verse praising כלב's different spirit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק where ה׳ praises כלב for having 'another spirit.' It fits the idea that כלב separated himself from the spies.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what is written: 'And My servant כלב, because there was another spirit with him, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the section with a פסוק that matches what it just taught about כלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says כלב had a 'different spirit' from the other spies. This supports רבא's teaching that כלב broke away from their plan. The praise is aimed at כלב specifically, which fits the idea that he had to work to stay apart, while יהושע was already protected.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is written

steps.whatToRemember: The names of the מרגלים hint at their sins. Only כלב went to חברון, to pray at the graves of the אבות. יהושע did not need to go because משה's prayer was built into his new name. The פסוק praising כלב's 'other spirit' fits this picture.

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
"And My servant Calev, because
there was another spirit with him, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports steps 10 and 11 with a פסוק about כלב.
steps.raayaObject: That כלב separated himself from the plan of the spies.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 14:24, which praises כלב for having 'another spirit.'

steps.title: What the names of the three giants mean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the names אחימן, ששי and תלמי as descriptions of how strong and heavy these giants were.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And there were אחימן, ששי and תלמי.' אחימן means he was the most skilled of his brothers. ששי means that when he walked he made the ground full of holes. תלמי means that when he walked he made the ground into rows of furrows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the פסוק and explains each giant's name as a hint to what he was like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name is read as a play on a Hebrew word. אחימן sounds like מיומן, meaning skilled. ששי sounds like שחתות, meaning holes, and תלמי sounds like תלמים, meaning furrows. These giants were so huge that their steps dented the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: The first giant; his name hints at being skilled
Furrows, the rows a plow cuts into a field

phrases.english: 'And there were Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, etc.'
'Ahiman': the most skilled among his brothers,
'Sheshai': because he would make the ground like pits,
'Talmai': because he would make the ground into furrows upon furrows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the same פסוק about the trip to חברון, now explaining who lived there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names of the giants describe their skill and their enormous size and weight.

steps.title: A second explanation: the giants built cities
steps.stepSummary: Another opinion says each giant built a city, and explains 'children of ענק' as meaning they were as tall as the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: אחימן built the city ענת, ששי built the city אלוש, and תלמי built the city תלבוש. They are called 'children of ענק' because they were so tall that the sun looked like a necklace on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different explanation of the giants' names, and then explains the phrase 'ילידי הענק.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this second explanation the names are linked to the cities each giant built, not to his body. The word ענק is read like עֲנָק, a necklace. They were so tall that the sun seemed to sit around their necks.

keyTerms.meaning: Children of ענק, the giants' family name

phrases.english: Another explanation: Ahiman built Anat,
Sheshai built Alush,
Talmai built Talbush.
'The children of Anak':
because they wore the sun like a necklace through their height.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second way to read the same three names from step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The giants' names refer to the cities they built, and 'ענק' describes their great height.

steps.title: What does 'חברון was built' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'built seven years before צוען' means, and shows that the plain reading does not make sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And חברון was built seven years before צוען.' What does 'built' mean? If you say it was really built first, would a father build a house for his younger son before his older son? It is written: 'The sons of חם were כוש, מצרים, פוט and כנען,' so כנען was the youngest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'נבנתה' means, and pushes back on the simple reading that חברון was physically built first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חברון is in the land of כנען, and צוען is in מצרים. Since כנען was a younger son of חם than מצרים, it makes no sense that his city would be built before his older brother's city. So 'built' must mean something else.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about how long it took to build חברון. The issue is the order: why would the younger brother's city be built before the older brother's?

phrases.english: 'And Hebron was built seven years [before Zoan of Egypt].'
What does 'was built' mean?
If you say it was literally built,

phrases.aramaic: אֶפְשָׁר אָדָם בּוֹנֶה בַּיִת לִבְנוֹ קָטָן
phrases.english: is it possible that a person builds a house for his younger son
before his older son?!
As it is written: 'And the sons of Ham: Cush, and Mizraim, etc.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 10:6. The פסוק goes on 'ופוט וכנען,' so כנען comes after מצרים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase of the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'נבנתה' means, since the literal meaning seems impossible.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal reading that חברון was physically built first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כנען was younger than מצרים, so his land would not be settled before his older brother's land.

steps.title: 'Built' means seven times more fruitful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'built' means חברון was seven times more developed and fruitful than צוען.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means that חברון was 'built up' seven times more than צוען.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer: the word 'built' here means fruitful and developed, not physically constructed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מבונה is read as 'built up,' meaning rich and productive. The 'seven' is no longer about years but about how many times better חברון was. This clears up the problem from step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: Built up, here meaning fruitful and productive

phrases.english: Rather, that it was built up
phrases.notes: Here 'built up' means rich and fruitful, not that someone put up buildings.

phrases.english: seven times more than Zoan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 by giving a non-literal meaning to 'built.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Built' means חברון was seven times more fruitful than צוען.

steps.title: How amazing it is that חברון beat צוען
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows how great ארץ ישראל is: even its rockiest place, חברון, was seven times better than the best place in the best land, צוען.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no rockier place in all of ארץ ישראל than חברון, because they bury the dead there. And there is no better land in the world than מצרים, as it says: 'Like the garden of ה׳, like the land of מצרים.' And there is no better place in all of מצרים than צוען, as it says: 'For his princes were in צוען.' And even so, חברון was seven times more fruitful than צוען.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by showing how big this comparison really is, using two פסוקים about מצרים and צוען.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חברון is the worst land in ארץ ישראל, and צוען is the best land in the best country. If the worst of ארץ ישראל beats the best of מצרים seven times over, then ארץ ישראל must be truly amazing. This is the praise of the land that the מרגלים saw with their own eyes.

keyTerms.meaning: The dead (literally, those who lie down)

steps.whatToRemember: 'חברון was built seven years before צוען' means that even rocky חברון was seven times more fruitful than צוען, the best spot in מצרים. This shows how special ארץ ישראל is.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the contrast with the מרגלים: they saw a land this good and still spoke badly about it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לְךָ טְרָשִׁים בְּכׇל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: And there is no rockier place in all of Eretz Yisrael
than Hebron,
because they bury the dead there.
phrases.notes: People buried their dead in rocky land that was no good for farming, so a burial place shows the ground is stony.

phrases.english: And there is none better among all the lands
than the land of Egypt,
as it is stated: 'Like the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לְךָ מְעוּלָּה בְּכׇל אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם
phrases.english: and there is none better in all the land of Egypt
than Zoan,
as it is written: 'For his princes were in Zoan,'
and even so, Hebron was built up
seven times more than Zoan.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לְךָ טְרָשִׁים בְּכׇל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל יָתֵר מֵחֶבְרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in step 16 by showing how impressive the comparison is.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that 'built' means חברון was seven times more fruitful than צוען, showing the greatness of ארץ ישראל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוקים 'כגן ה׳ כארץ מצרים' and 'כי היו בצען שריו,' plus the fact that חברון was a burial place.

steps.title: Challenge: חברון produced the best sheep, so how can it be rocky?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how חברון can be rocky land, when a פסוק and a ברייתא show that the best sheep came from חברון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is חברון really rocky? It says that אבשלום asked the king to let him go to חברון, and רב אויא (or רבה בר בר חנן) explained that he went to bring sheep from there. A ברייתא also teaches that rams come from מואב and sheep come from חברון. So חברון must have rich land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last step, which called חברון the rockiest place in ארץ ישראל. It brings proof that חברון was famous for raising excellent sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea behind the question is that fat, healthy animals need rich land. If חברון produced the choicest sheep, even good enough for קרבנות, its land should be good, not rocky. That seems to contradict calling חברון the rockiest spot.

keyTerms.meaning: Rocky, stony ground that is hard to farm
But isn't it written? A way of bringing a פסוק to challenge an idea
And some say. Used when it is unclear which אמורא said something
And it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And is Hebron really rocky land?
But isn't it written:
"And it came to pass at the end of forty years,
that Absalom said to the king:
Please let me go, etc."
phrases.notes: The rest of the פסוק says he wants to go to חברון to keep a vow he made.

phrases.english: And Rav Avya said,
and some say it was Rabba bar bar Chanan:
This means he went to bring sheep from Hebron.
And it was taught in a ברייתא:
Rams come from Moab,
and sheep come from Hebron!
phrases.notes: These were the places known for the best animals to bring as קרבנות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 17 that חברון was the rockiest place in ארץ ישראל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement that חברון was rocky land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Famous high-quality sheep suggest rich land, which contradicts calling חברון rocky.

steps.title: Answer: Thin soil grows grass that fattens animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the sheep actually prove חברון is rocky: thin soil only grows grazing grass, which fattens livestock.
steps.simpleTranslation: From that very source we see it. Because the soil is thin, it is only good for pasture, and that makes the animals fat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by turning it around. The same fact that seemed to prove rich land actually proves thin, rocky land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land with thin soil cannot grow grain or fruit trees, so it is left as pasture. Grass grows there, and the animals that graze on it become fat. So excellent sheep fit perfectly with חברון being rocky land.

keyTerms.meaning: From it. From that very source we can prove our point

steps.whatToRemember: חברון's fame for sheep does not argue against its rocky soil. Thin soil grows only grass, which is exactly what makes sheep fat. So the story still shows how great ארץ ישראל is, since even its rockiest place was seven times better than צוען.

phrases.english: From that very source we can prove it:
since the soil is thin,
it is used as pasture,
and the livestock grow fat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by showing that its evidence supports the claim of rocky land.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turning the proof around: the evidence actually supports the original claim.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Fat sheep mean the land is rich, so חברון cannot be rocky.
steps.terutzMaskana: Thin, rocky soil is good only for grazing, and grazing fattens sheep. So חברון was rocky and still produced the best sheep.

steps.title: The next פסוק: The spies return from scouting the land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק about the מרגלים coming back, to begin explaining it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "And they returned from spying out the land."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next discussion. It quotes the next פסוק in the story of the מרגלים, and the explanation comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The talk about חברון is finished, and the גמרא goes back to explaining the פסוקים of the spies one by one. Here it only opens the quote. The teaching about it comes on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: "And they returned from spying out the land
phrases.notes: במדבר 13:25. The פסוק continues: "at the end of forty days."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the חברון discussion to the next פסוק in the story of the מרגלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the פסוק about the spies' return so the גמרא can explain it next.
